Okay, so I'm trying to figure out why Jerry's ball followed a curved path and fell to the ground. The options given are A) air friction stopped the ball, B) gravity changed the ball's direction, C) the ball wasn't thrown hard enough, and D) the ball wasn't thrown straight up.

First, I remember from school that when you throw a ball straight up, it goes up and then comes back down. That's because of gravity pulling it back down. So, the curved path is because of gravity, not air resistance. But I'm not entirely sure if air resistance plays any role at all.

I think about what happens when you throw a ball. If there was no air resistance, the path would be a perfect parabola. But in real life, air resistance does have some effect, making the path a bit more curved or flatter, but the main reason for the curve is still gravity. So, air resistance is a secondary factor, not the primary cause.

Looking at the options, A says air friction stopped the ball. That doesn't sound right because air resistance would slow it down, but it wouldn't make it fall straight down. The ball would just have a more curved path but still go up and then come back. So A is probably not the correct answer.

Option B says gravity changed the ball's direction. That makes sense because gravity pulls the ball downward, making it curve as it falls. So B seems correct.

Option C says the ball wasn't thrown hard enough. If it wasn't thrown hard, it might not go as high, but it would still follow a curved path and fall because of gravity. So C doesn't explain why it fell to the ground specifically.

Option D says the ball wasn't thrown straight up. If it wasn't thrown straight up, it would still follow a curved path because gravity affects it in the vertical direction regardless of the horizontal component. So D doesn't explain the fall either.

Putting it all together, the main reason the ball followed a curved path and fell is because gravity changed its direction, making B the correct answer.
